tools.name: how_to_verify_income
tools.description: Explains how to check or verify a person’s income (a tenant, applicant, borrower, guarantor, investor, or yourself), including bank-based income analysis, pay stubs, and their limits. Use when someone asks how to verify, check, or prove income.

tools.name: start_income_verification
tools.description: Returns the link and steps to request a bank-based income report from Income Checker for a tenant, applicant, borrower, or yourself. Use when the user wants to actually verify or check someone’s income, not just learn how.

tools.name: monthly_income_from_pay
tools.description: Converts a pay amount (hourly, weekly, every two weeks, twice a month, monthly, or annual) into gross monthly, annual, biweekly, weekly, and hourly income.

tools.name: rent_to_income
tools.description: Income needed for a given rent (2.5x, 3x, 3.5x rules), the max rent for a given income at 3x, or the rent-to-income ratio when both are given. Pass monthly figures.

tools.name: rent_affordability
tools.description: Affordable rent from gross monthly income using the 30% rule, the 3x-rent rule, a 25-30% comfortable range capped at 36% total debt, and 50/30/20.

tools.name: debt_to_income
tools.description: Front-end (housing) and back-end debt-to-income ratios with common lender bands.

tools.name: prorated_rent
tools.description: Rent owed for a partial first month, from the move-in date through the end of that month.

tools.name: check_pay_stub_math
tools.description: Checks the figures on a pay stub for internal inconsistencies: gross minus deductions vs net, hours × rate, Social Security and Medicare rates, pay period length, pay date, year-to-date totals, and suspiciously round numbers. Read the numbers off the stub and pass them in. Flags items for follow-up;

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Shows the signed-in user’s email and how many verification credits they have left.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Creates a secure Stripe checkout link for a pack of non-expiring verification credits. Packs: 1 for $5.00, 3 for $15.00, 5 for $25.00, 10 for $50.00, 25 for $125.00, 50 for $250.00. Give the user the link to pay; credits are added once payment completes.

tools.name: send_verification_request
tools.description: Uses one credit to create a bank-based income check and emails the applicant a secure link to connect their bank through Plaid. Confirm the applicant’s name and email with the user before calling. The report is ready after the applicant connects; check it with list_verifications or get_report.

tools.name: list_verifications
tools.description: Lists the signed-in user’s income verification requests, newest first, with status and report links.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Returns the income analysis for a completed verification: estimated monthly income, income sources, other deposits, and account balances. Present figures as estimates, never as verified or approved income.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_verification_request" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Uses one credit to create a bank-based income check and emails the applicant a secure link to connect their bank through Plaid. Confirm the applicant’s name and…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, send_verification_request · Private data: check_pay_stub_math · Public sink: get_account, send_verification_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, send_verification_request · Private data: check_pay_stub_math · Public sink: get_account, send_verification_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
